stories.title: Brazil's leftist President Lula wins fourth term in dramatic comeback
summary: Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched a re-election victory, but his rival Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to annul the vote.
With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries — such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru — all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump.
The senator is the son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year jail term for attempting a coup after his loss to Lula in the country’s last election in 2022.

stories.title: Punjab CM orders completion of 5,734 water filtration plants by June 2027
summary: LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has directed the completion of 5,734 water filtration plants by June 2027, reiterating that access to clean drinking water is a fundamental right of every citizen.
Chairing a meeting of the Punjab Saaf Pani Authority, the chief minister assigned the responsibility of monitoring water filtration plants to the respective assistant commissioners.
Each mobile workshop will have plumbers and other technical staff to ensure timely maintenance of the plants and people’s uninterrupted access to clean drinking water.

stories.title: Heavy penalties, fees for illegal housing schemes recommended in Lahore Division Master Plan-2050
summary: Currently, matters concerning city planning are being dealt with under the obsolete amended Lahore Division Plan-2016 - a revised version of the Punjab Capital Master Plan 2004-2021.
The Lahore Division Master Plan-2050 was completed in 2022 and later challenged in the Lahore High Court that finally suspended its enforcement in January 2023.
The master plan includes a regional plan of Lahore division, as well as master plans of major urban settlements falling within the division.

summary: BAHAWALPUR: A police constable along with his four accomplices has been booked for allegedly torturing a woman to death at Mauza Muhammad Naich in the limits of Bahawalpur Channigoth police on Sunday.
Meanwhile, Lodhran DPO Beenish Fatima has dismissed Lodhran police front desk head Bilal Parvez from service for alleged misconduct and irregularities.

BCCI POLLS: The Bahawalpur Saddar police have booked fifteen unidentified suspects for storming and ransacking the Bahawalpur Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCI) building and tampering with the sealed ballot boxes.

stories.title: Experts call for preventive measures as dengue cases continue to rise in KP
summary: PESHAWAR: The cases of dengue fever continued to rise in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during October, the peak month for infection, with the provincial tally reaching 4,856 after 51 new cases were reported on Sunday.

The latest dengue situation report, released by Integrated Diseases Surveillance and Response System (IDSRS) at Directorate General Health Services of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, shows that 2,244 cases have been reported during the current month.
Health officials said that October had traditionally been the most infectious period of the year as the highest number of dengue cases were reported during that month.

stories.title: Fire at fuel station in Larkana causes widespread destruction
summary: LARKANA: A fuel station was completely destroyed and many vehicles were reduced to ashes in a fire that broke out at the facility along Empire Road in Larkana during the night intervening Saturday and Sunday.

Officials at the Market police station said that the preliminary inquiry into the incident suggested that the fire had started from the oil tanker, which was filling the underground fuel tank of the station.
Initial findings, however, suggested that a spark in the engine section of the oil tanker triggered the fire that engulfed the entire station and whatever was present at the site.

stories.title: Residents turn to alternative fuel amid gas shortages and rising LPG prices in twin cities
summary: Most of the people have started using wood and coal as the prices of LPG cylinders have reached Rs600 per kg against Rs279 per kg fixed by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

On the other hand, the Sui Natural Gas Pipelines (SNGPL) has stopped providing LPG cylinders to domestic and commercial consumers for the last two months and private companies are selling it at higher prices to cash in on the situation.

LPG not available and SNGPL has stopped supply of cylinders in twin cities, says official The price of an 11kg domestic gas cylinder has reached Rs6,500, while commercial cylinders are available at over Rs25,000.

stories.title: Two more handcuffed suspects killed by accomplices in Islamabad: police
summary: The police public relations branch said the suspects, Afghan nationals, were arrested in connection with an incident in which a 23-year-old woman was injured while resisting a gang rape attempt by robbers in a park on October 12.
In response, a police team took the handcuffed suspects to a junkyard in Rawal Town.

Sources in the police said the suspects were arrested in connection with the case registered on October 12 at the Secretariat police station under sections 394, 375-A and 511 of Pakistan Penal Code in response to a complaint lodged by the woman.

summary: He opposed any commercial activity along Nehr-i-Khayyam and demanded that the Sindh government make the project’s PC-1, Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report and other relevant documents public.
Mr Saifuddin said Nehr-i-Khayyam was originally a natural waterway that carried rainwater but had gradually been turned into a sewerage channel.
Mr Saifuddin called for a technical review of the project to assess its potential impact on the city’s drainage system and ensure proper arrangements for sewage disposal and maintenance.

stories.title: JUI-F vows to keep fighting for constitutional supremacy
summary: QUETTA: JUI-F Balochistan chief Maulana Abdul Wasey said on Sunday that his party was being punished for upholding the supremacy of the Constitution, protecting democratic values and pursuing a peaceful political struggle.
However, he said it was regrettable that despite these resources, the province’s people continued to be “deprived of basic facilities, including gas”.

The JUI-F provincial chief said “depriving the people of Balochistan of their fundamental rights” and “denying them a fair share” of the benefits generated from the province’s resources was “unacceptable”.

stories.title: Pakistan’s global role
summary: One set of views sees Pakistan as a client state of the US, that is, one that’s subservient to America’s imperial interests and its immediate allies in the region, the Gulf monarchies.
However, in an effort to account for Pakistan’s global and regional behaviour, these observations lapse back to the rather broad and imprecise categories of ‘client state’ or ‘fundamentalist state’.

What is consistent though is the subordinate role that the state here plays in global affairs, not just in terms of geopolitics but also — and more fundamentally — in terms of international economic processes.

stories.title: Season of protests
summary: In Italy, students, farmers and truckers took to the streets in protests driven by education costs, economic grievances, and anti-war sentiment.
In India, the youth ‘Cockroach’ movement has spearheaded the protests and mounted the most significant challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government so far.
More generally, youth-led protests may force governments to take more seriously the needs and aspirations of young people which have rarely been a priority.

stories.title: Lahore doctor’s penalty in death case set aside
summary: Tribunal orders fresh probe into post-surgery death in 2021 The tribunal allowed the appeal of senior anaesthetist Dr Muhammad Sheraz Saleem and ordered that his case be reconsidered.
It said several questions remained unresolved, including the timing of the medical emergency, interpretation of footage, the accuracy of recorded times and doctors’ responsibilities.

The tribunal also partly allowed an appeal by the child’s father, Umer Farooq, directing the regulator to reconsider his complaints against specific practitioners after providing him an opportunity to respond.

stories.title: Wheat price dilemma
summary: THE announcement of an indicative wheat price of Rs4,500 per 40 kilograms may have come too late for Sindh farmers, but it is welcome as far as it goes.
Since April 2025, when the government dropped the support price and suspended large-scale procurement, farmers have been promised a market-based system that would serve them better.
It is whether the system that replaces government buying shares the risk fairly among farmers, traders, millers, banks, and the state, keeps flour affordable, and protects the country’s food supply.

stories.title: VIEWPOINT: Auto policy’s tax paradox
summary: Low tax rates matter, but defining the policy is also crucial Both sides of the current argument are partly right.
The concessional 8.5pc sales tax on most hybrids expired on June 30 with the expiry of the last auto industry development and export policy, causing taxes on locally made hybrids to jump to 25pc.
Low taxes in the early years build the market: China exempted electric cars from purchase tax for nearly a decade, and Norway waived VAT before both began phased rollbacks.

stories.title: Brewing crisis of shrinking farm size
summary: Yet another structural problem – the subdivision of agricultural land into smaller and scattered holdings – is worsening silently.

For farms, smaller and increasingly dispersed holdings make mechanisation next to impossible, raise cultivation and supervision costs, limit access to credit and modern technologies, and reduce farmers’ capacity to generate marketable surpluses and cash for themselves.
It is also necessary because subdivision of agricultural land is not merely a farming problem; it is also a question of rural livelihoods and national poverty.

stories.title: FBR reforms, again?
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s warning against resistance to tax reforms has once again put a spotlight on the efforts to restructure the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR).
The reforms introduced partial automation, universal self-assessment and the transfer of sales tax and federal excise administration from Customs to Inland Revenue.

The question is whether artificial intelligence, digital invoicing, production monitoring and automated risk assessment can improve tax compliance without stronger audit procedures and enforcement accountability.

stories.title: GB launches subsidised wheat seeds scheme
summary: GB Agri­culture, Livestock and Fish­eries Secretary Usman Ahmed told Dawn that the GB government has taken another step towards making the region self-sufficie­nt in agriculture and for the welfare of local farmers.

Under the Chief Min­ister’s Vision for Agric­ult­ure, the government is providing quality, certified whe­at seeds to farmers across the region at a 50 per cent subsidy on the special directives of Chief Minister Amjad Hussain.
Under the initiative, hi­gh-quality, certified wheat seeds will be procured from Punjab and distributed among farmers in all districts of GB, he said.

stories.title: DPM Dar, Chinese envoy review CPEC progress
summary: ISLAMABAD: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong on Sunday to review progress on the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor and reaffirm bilateral ties, the Foreign Office said.

Dar also emphasised the need for sustained high-level engagements to build what officials term a “Pakistan-China Community of Shared Future in the New Era.” Beyond economic and bilateral initiatives, the two diplomats discussed recent regional developments.

In August, officials said the corridor’s first phase had attracted approximately $25 billion in Chinese investment, while the next phase would prioritise private-sector partnerships and technology transfer.

stories.title: Mother can’t be denied child’s custody over second marriage, rules PHC
summary: While disposing of a revision petition of a resident of Kohat, the bench declined to grant him custody of his minor son, but allowed him visitation rights.
The trial court on Oct 16, 2025, partially allowed the petition and granted custody of the minor to the petitioner, while preserving the visitation rights of the minor’s mother.

In these circumstances, an abrupt transfer of custody to the petitioner, without first establishing a meaningful relationship between father and son, would risk disturbing the minor’s emotional security and settled routine,” the bench observed.

stories.title: Special polio drive in Peshawar’s high-risk UCs begins today
summary: PESHAWAR: The District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC) has completed preparations for a six-day special polio booster dose campaign in 48 high-risk union councils of Peshawar, targeting 1,111,107 children aged four months to 10 years from today (Monday).
Children aged five to 10 years in the targeted union councils will also receive oral polio vaccine drops.
Peshawar deputy commissioner Afaq Wazir has urged parents to ensure that their children aged four months to 10 years receive the booster dose to protect them from lifelong disability caused by polio.

stories.title: Crime in Punjab cut by 63pc in Sept, claims CCD
summary: LAHORE: The Crime Control Department (CCD) has released a comparison of crime figures of September 2023-24 and September 2025-26, claiming 63pc reduction in overall crime, including robbery and motorcycle theft, across the province.
Similarly, Multan region recorded a 59pc while Gujranwala and Bahawalpur regions each recorded a 58pc decrease in crime.
Sheikhupura region showed a 57pc cut, Sargodha 56pc, Rawalpindi 52pc and Dera Ghazi Khan region recorded a 43pc decrease in the crime rate.

stories.title: Khuhro rules out possibility of any new province in Sindh
summary: LARKANA: Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Sindh president Nisar Ahmed Khuhro said on Sunday that the Sindh Assembly, by unanimously passing a resolution against new provinces, had constitutionally closed the path to the creation of a new province in Sindh.

A new province could be formed only if the relevant assembly passed a resolution with a two-thirds majority, he said, adding that the Sindh Assembly had already ruled that the province did not need one by passing a resolution against new provinces and administrative units.
The same assembly had passed the resolution that led to the creation of Pakistan, he noted, and had now passed resolutions against new provinces six times.

stories.title: Pakistan’s food supply fails own dietary guidelines: FAO
summary: FAO’s new policy brief, “Food Supply for Healthy Diets in Pakistan,” says ensuring equitable access to diverse, nutritious, safe and affordable foods is a policy imperative, particularly as more than 60 per cent of Pakistanis cannot afford a healthy diet.
Pakistan adopted its food-based dietary guidelines in 2018, setting out evidence-based recommendations for the types and quantities of foods needed for healthy diets.
The report identifies persistent shortages in several nutritious food groups, particularly vegetables, roots and tubers, fruits, and legumes and pulses.

stories.title: Pakistan, Qatar explore new avenues for trade, investment cooperation
summary: The commitment was expressed during the second meeting of the Pakistan-Qatar Joint Task Force (JTF) on Trade and Investment, co-chaired by Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan and Qatar’s Minister of State for Foreign Trade Affairs Dr Ahmad bin Mohammed Al-Sayed in Doha.

Investment Fund Pakistan further presented the concept of an Investment Fund, highlighting opportunities for Qatari participation in infrastructure, agriculture, industrial development, information technology and other priority sectors.
To translate the discussions into practical outcomes, Pakistan called for the early operationalisation of 11 Technical Working Groups identified during the first Joint Task Force meeting.

stories.title: Israel to close all West Bank crossings on election day
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to exact a heavy price for the attack just days before polls and said he was planning an operation on a scale not seen since Israel first occupied the West Bank in 1967.
Israel’s longest serving prime minister Netanyahu is facing a tight race for a new term in Tuesday’s polls, with his security-first reputation all but shattered by the Oct 7, 2023 attack.

Strike on university Meanwhile, an Israeli strike on a university in Gaza City killed three people on Sunday, staff and a local hospital said, while the civil defence agency reported four others killed elsewhere in the territory.

stories.title: Govt moves to establish new ‘umbrella’ privatisation entity
summary: Therefore, the government’s pol­icy decision was needed for establishing a single institutional framework and mechanism for carrying out privatisation and public private partnership transactions in an efficient manner.

For this, it seeks to reconstitute the Privatisation Commission as the Privatisation and Public-Private Partnership Commission, to repeal the Public Private Partnership Authority Act 2017 and dissolve the P3A.

The draft claims that it provides a comprehensive legal framework for public private partnerships, including the contractual framework for PPP agreements, a federal PPP pipeline, the approval process, the risk management unit and PPP transaction execution committees.

stories.title: Flights resume at Riyadh airport after two-week closure as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia
summary: Flights resumed at Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday following a series of deadly attacks on the facility that saw it closed for two weeks, even as Yemen’s Houthi rebels targeted the country with strikes.

Alerts warning of possible attacks were activated across the kingdom’s south throughout the day, with the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis saying at least 10 ballistic missiles were intercepted.
The attacks came after the Houthi fighters said that — in the space of 24 hours — they targeted three Saudi airports, including in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base.

stories.title: KP Governor Kundi says Sohail Afridi, assembly speaker 'in safe hands' after house arrest
summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Sunday that Sohail Afridi and Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati were “in safe hands” after being placed under house arrest.

Appearing on Geo News’ TV programme ‘Jirga’ aired on Sunday night, the governor — who now runs the province — was asked about the whereabouts of Afridi, Kundi said he had been placed under house arrest and was “in safe hands — there is no need to worry”.
Asked why Afridi was not being released if there were no cases against him, Kundi replied he could provide an update tomorrow regarding the matter.
